waste_flags.message: Flood irrigation on corn loses about 21 acre-ft per year compared with drip.
Flood irrigation on oats loses about 2.1 acre-ft per year compared with drip.

assumptions: Mature, full-producing orchards.
Weather is regional (NASA POWER grid cell about 50 km wide).
Yield losses from weather and water only. Nutrients, pests, and disease are assumed well managed.
Reference ET0 is FAO-56 Penman-Monteith from NASA POWER daily weather.
Crop water use is ETc = Kc x ET0 with the FAO-56 single crop coefficient curve.
Effective rain: rain under 5 mm in a day is lost, and 80 percent of larger rains reach the root zone (Dastane 1974, FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 25).
Irrigation refills the root zone when half of the available water is used (FAO-56 soil water balance). The root zone starts each season full.
Relative yield uses FAO-33: 1 - Ya/Ym = Ky x (1 - ETa/ETc). Each heat stress day above this location's normal count takes another 0.25 percent off, up to 10 percent.
Seasons that cross the new year are counted in the year they end.
Dormant orchards and alfalfa are not irrigated outside their growing season.
Some crop parameters are placeholders still being checked against FAO sources: almonds, corn, oats, processing_tomatoes.
Almond yield uses the statewide median (no county data for Merced).
Walnut yield uses the statewide median (no county data for Merced).
Alfalfa hay yield uses the statewide median (no county data for Merced).
Almond production cost uses the Sacramento Valley study (no study for San Joaquin Valley North).
Walnut production cost uses the Sacramento Valley study (no study for San Joaquin Valley North).
Processing tomato production cost uses the San Joaquin Valley South study (no study for San Joaquin Valley North).
No production cost study for oat in any region, so it has no production cost.
Surface water price uses a typical Merced Irrigation District value. Actual district rates vary.
Cost estimate: The Sacramento Valley study prices no drip system; the San Joaquin Valley South 2024 study's system cost is used.
Cost estimate: National/regional ERS average; no California oats cost study available.
Cost estimate: National ERS average; no California oats cost study..
Revenue uses the same median-normalized harvest quantity as the harvest-weight display.
Prices: each year uses that year's USDA NASS price.
Costs: each year's UC Davis study costs are scaled to that year by USDA NASS prices-paid indexes and U.S. EIA diesel and electricity prices.
Applied water is 35% surface water at $50 per acre-ft and 65% groundwater pumped from 150 ft (about $39 per acre-ft at 2016 electricity prices).
The summary's high, low, and typical years are ranked by farm profit.
Harvest weight is the selected county or statewide median yield scaled by how each year's relative yield compares with this block's median year, so a typical year shows a typical county harvest.
Frost occurred within 45 days of planting in 5 of 5 years for block b4 (oats planted in Nov).

summary.avg_cost.label: Estimated cost per year
summary.avg_cost.formula_text: Sum of yearly farm cost / number of years with price data, 2012 to 2016

inputs.name: Farm cost, 2012
inputs.source: Calculated each year as inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system. Inputs, harvest and irrigation system come from the cost studies (Almonds: UC Davis Cost and Return Study, Almonds, Sacramento Valley, 2024, p. 19 (used because San Joaquin Valley North has no almonds study); Processing tomatoes: UC Davis Cost and Return Study, Processing tomatoes, San Joaquin Valley South, 2018, p. 14 (used because San Joaquin Valley North has no processing tomatoes study); Corn: UC Davis Cost and Return Study, Corn, San Joaquin Valley North, 2015, p. 11; Oats: USDA ERS Commodity Costs and Returns, oats, U.S. total (no California study)), scaled to that year's input prices (nearest year when missing) by the USDA NASS Prices Paid Index (2011=100) and the U.S. EIA diesel price, times acres (harvest times simulated tons). Water is the acre-ft applied (YieldGenerator simulation using NASA POWER weather, NASA POWER weather, grid cell 37.5, -120.625, 2012 to 2016) priced at Merced Irrigation District 2024 rate ($50/acre-ft); 2022 drought rate was $100/acre-ft for surface water and at the U.S. EIA California commercial electricity price for well pumping.

block.b1.2012.profit.label: Estimated margin, Almonds, 2012
block.b1.2012.profit.formula_text: Sales (harvest x price) - cost, where cost = inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system
block.b1.2012.profit.rounding: Harvest to 0.01 ton, index ratios to 0.000001, acre-ft to 0.0001, each cost part to $0.01, cost to $1. Sales to $1.

steps.text: Harvest: 1,960 lb/acre / 2,000 lb/ton x 1 / 1 x 40 acres = 39.20 tons
Sales: 39.20 tons x 2,000 lb/ton x $2.58 per lb = $202,272
NASS fertilizer index ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: 101.4 / 101.2 = 1.001976
NASS chemicals index ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: 105.4 / 117 = 0.900855
NASS wage rate index ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: 102.9 / 171 = 0.601754
EIA diesel price ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: $3.968 / $3.76 = 1.055319
Harvest and haul dollars per acre in the study: $622.7273 per ton x 1.1 tons = $685.00003
Inputs cost: $2,074.33 per acre x 40 acres = $82,973.20
Harvest cost: 39.20 tons x $622.7273 per ton x 1.055319 diesel ratio = $25,761.297299, rounded to $25,761.30
Irrigation system (drip) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $1,800 / 23 = $78.26087, rounded to $78.2609
Irrigation system cost (drip, installed cost / life): $78.2609 per acre per year x 0.907305 weighted ratio x 40 acres = $2,840.260235, rounded to $2,840.26
Surface water: 138.5915 acre-ft x 0.35 = 48.507025 acre-ft, rounded to 48.5070 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 48.5070 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $2,425.35
Groundwater: 138.5915 acre-ft x 0.65 = 90.084475 acre-ft, rounded to 90.0845 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 90.0845 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1341 per kWh = $3,092.564851, rounded to $3,092.56
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $2,425.35 + groundwater pumping $3,092.56 = $5,517.91
Cost: inputs $82,973.20 + harvest $25,761.30 + water $5,517.91 + irrigation system $2,840.26 = $117,092.67, rounded to $117,093

block.b1.2012.cost.label: Estimated cost, Almonds, 2012
block.b1.2012.cost.formula_text: Cost = inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system
block.b1.2012.cost.rounding: Harvest to 0.01 ton, index ratios to 0.000001, acre-ft to 0.0001, each cost part to $0.01, cost to $1.

steps.text: NASS fertilizer index ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: 101.4 / 101.2 = 1.001976
NASS chemicals index ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: 105.4 / 117 = 0.900855
NASS wage rate index ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: 102.9 / 171 = 0.601754
EIA diesel price ratio, 2012 / 2024 study year: $3.968 / $3.76 = 1.055319
Harvest and haul dollars per acre in the study: $622.7273 per ton x 1.1 tons = $685.00003
Inputs cost: $2,074.33 per acre x 40 acres = $82,973.20
Harvest cost: 39.2 tons x $622.7273 per ton x 1.055319 diesel ratio = $25,761.297299, rounded to $25,761.30
Irrigation system (drip) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $1,800 / 23 = $78.26087, rounded to $78.2609
Irrigation system cost (drip, installed cost / life): $78.2609 per acre per year x 0.907305 weighted ratio x 40 acres = $2,840.260235, rounded to $2,840.26
Surface water: 138.5915 acre-ft x 0.35 = 48.507025 acre-ft, rounded to 48.5070 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 48.5070 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $2,425.35
Groundwater: 138.5915 acre-ft x 0.65 = 90.084475 acre-ft, rounded to 90.0845 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 90.0845 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1341 per kWh = $3,092.564851, rounded to $3,092.56
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $2,425.35 + groundwater pumping $3,092.56 = $5,517.91
Cost: inputs $82,973.20 + harvest $25,761.30 + water $5,517.91 + irrigation system $2,840.26 = $117,092.67, rounded to $117,093

block.b1.2015.profit.label: Estimated margin, Almonds, 2015
block.b1.2015.profit.formula_text: Sales (harvest x price) - cost, where cost = inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system
block.b1.2015.profit.rounding: Harvest to 0.01 ton, index ratios to 0.000001, acre-ft to 0.0001, each cost part to $0.01, cost to $1. Sales to $1.

steps.text: Harvest: 1,960 lb/acre / 2,000 lb/ton x 1 / 1 x 40 acres = 39.20 tons
Sales: 39.20 tons x 2,000 lb/ton x $3.13 per lb = $245,392
NASS fertilizer index ratio, 2015 / 2024 study year: 87.2 / 101.2 = 0.861660
NASS chemicals index ratio, 2015 / 2024 study year: 106.5 / 117 = 0.910256
NASS wage rate index ratio, 2015 / 2024 study year: 111.9 / 171 = 0.654386
EIA diesel price ratio, 2015 / 2024 study year: $2.707 / $3.76 = 0.719947
Harvest and haul dollars per acre in the study: $622.7273 per ton x 1.1 tons = $685.00003
Inputs cost: $1,900.96 per acre x 40 acres = $76,038.40
Harvest cost: 39.20 tons x $622.7273 per ton x 0.719947 diesel ratio = $17,574.561537, rounded to $17,574.56
Irrigation system (drip) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $1,800 / 23 = $78.26087, rounded to $78.2609
Irrigation system cost (drip, installed cost / life): $78.2609 per acre per year x 0.776556 weighted ratio x 40 acres = $2,430.958858, rounded to $2,430.96
Surface water: 138.9582 acre-ft x 0.35 = 48.63537 acre-ft, rounded to 48.6354 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 48.6354 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $2,431.77
Groundwater: 138.9582 acre-ft x 0.65 = 90.32283 acre-ft, rounded to 90.3228 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 90.3228 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1573 per kWh = $3,637.190769, rounded to $3,637.19
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $2,431.77 + groundwater pumping $3,637.19 = $6,068.96
Cost: inputs $76,038.40 + harvest $17,574.56 + water $6,068.96 + irrigation system $2,430.96 = $102,112.88, rounded to $102,113

steps.text: NASS seeds index ratio, 2014 / 2018 study year: 113.5 / 115.6 = 0.981834

Surface water: 285.8246 acre-ft x 0.35 = 100.03861 acre-ft, rounded to 100.0386 acre-ft

Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $5,001.93 + groundwater pumping $7,429.06 = $12,430.99

block.b3.2014.profit.label: Estimated margin, Corn, 2014
block.b3.2014.profit.formula_text: Sales (harvest x price) - cost, where cost = inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system
block.b3.2014.profit.rounding: Harvest to 0.01 ton, index ratios to 0.000001, acre-ft to 0.0001, each cost part to $0.01, cost to $1. Sales to $1.

steps.text: Harvest: 156.3 bu/acre x 56 lb/bu / 2,000 lb/ton x 1 / 1 x 15 acres = 65.646 tons, rounded to 65.65 tons
Sales: 65.65 tons x 2,000 lb/ton / 56 lb/bu x $4.81 per bu = $11,277.732143, rounded to $11,278
NASS seeds index ratio, 2014 / 2015 study year: 113.5 / 124.6 = 0.910915
NASS fertilizer index ratio, 2014 / 2015 study year: 94.5 / 87.2 = 1.083716
NASS chemicals index ratio, 2014 / 2015 study year: 109.5 / 106.5 = 1.028169
NASS wage rate index ratio, 2014 / 2015 study year: 108 / 111.9 = 0.965147
EIA diesel price ratio, 2014 / 2015 study year: $3.825 / $2.707 = 1.413003

Weighted ratio for costs with no index of their own (other inputs, irrigation system): ($67 x 0.910915 + $230 x 1.083716 + $44 x 1.028169 + $173 x 0.965147 + $131 x 1.413003) / ($67 + $230 + $44 + $173 + $131) = 1.097053
Inputs cost: $789.88 per acre x 15 acres = $11,848.20
Harvest cost: 65.65 tons x $0 per ton (no separate harvest line) = $0.00
Irrigation system (flood) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $9 / 15 + $1 / 15 = $0.666667, rounded to $0.6667
Irrigation system cost (flood, installed cost / life): $0.6667 per acre per year x 1.097053 weighted ratio x 15 acres = $10.971079, rounded to $10.97
Surface water: 61.5894 acre-ft x 0.35 = 21.55629 acre-ft, rounded to 21.5563 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 21.5563 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $1,077.815, rounded to $1,077.82
Groundwater: 61.5894 acre-ft x 0.65 = 40.03311 acre-ft, rounded to 40.0331 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 40.0331 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1562 per kWh = $1,600.811576, rounded to $1,600.81
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $1,077.82 + groundwater pumping $1,600.81 = $2,678.63
Cost: inputs $11,848.20 + harvest $0.00 + water $2,678.63 + irrigation system $10.97 = $14,537.80, rounded to $14,538

block.b3.2016.cost.label: Estimated cost, Corn, 2016
block.b3.2016.cost.formula_text: Cost = inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system

steps.text: NASS seeds index ratio, 2016 / 2015 study year: 121.4 / 124.6 = 0.974318
NASS fertilizer index ratio, 2016 / 2015 study year: 71.8 / 87.2 = 0.823394
NASS chemicals index ratio, 2016 / 2015 study year: 107.7 / 106.5 = 1.011268
NASS wage rate index ratio, 2016 / 2015 study year: 115.9 / 111.9 = 1.035746
EIA diesel price ratio, 2016 / 2015 study year: $2.304 / $2.707 = 0.851127

Weighted ratio for costs with no index of their own (other inputs, irrigation system): ($67 x 0.974318 + $230 x 0.823394 + $44 x 1.011268 + $173 x 1.035746 + $131 x 0.851127) / ($67 + $230 + $44 + $173 + $131) = 0.914477
Inputs cost: $658.42 per acre x 15 acres = $9,876.30
Harvest cost: 65.65 tons x $0 per ton (no separate harvest line) = $0.00
Irrigation system (flood) per acre per year, installed cost / life: $9 / 15 + $1 / 15 = $0.666667, rounded to $0.6667
Irrigation system cost (flood, installed cost / life): $0.6667 per acre per year x 0.914477 weighted ratio x 15 acres = $9.145227, rounded to $9.15
Surface water: 61.5244 acre-ft x 0.35 = 21.53354 acre-ft, rounded to 21.5335 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 21.5335 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $1,076.675, rounded to $1,076.68
Groundwater: 61.5244 acre-ft x 0.65 = 39.99086 acre-ft, rounded to 39.9909 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 39.9909 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1507 per kWh = $1,542.816929, rounded to $1,542.82
Water cost (35% surface water, 65% wells): surface water $1,076.68 + groundwater pumping $1,542.82 = $2,619.50
Cost: inputs $9,876.30 + harvest $0.00 + water $2,619.50 + irrigation system $9.15 = $12,504.95, rounded to $12,505

steps.text: Harvest: 86.6 bu/acre x 32 lb/bu / 2,000 lb/ton x 1 / 1 x 12 acres = 16.6272 tons, rounded to 16.63 tons
Sales: 16.63 tons x 2,000 lb/ton / 32 lb/bu x $4.15 per bu = $4,313.40625, rounded to $4,313
Inputs per acre (that year's USDA ERS values, not index scaled): $15.76 + $51.78 + $2.45 + $38.12 + $12.64 = $120.75
Inputs cost: $120.75 per acre x 12 acres = $1,449.00
Harvest cost: 16.63 tons x $0 per ton (no separate harvest line) = $0.00
Irrigation system cost (flood) (USDA ERS whole-farm average per planted acre already includes these costs; no separate irrigation system line): $0 per acre per year x 12 acres = $0.00
Surface water: 6.5165 acre-ft x 0.35 = 2.280775 acre-ft, rounded to 2.2808 acre-ft
Surface water cost: 2.2808 acre-ft x $50 per acre-ft = $114.04
Groundwater: 6.5165 acre-ft x 0.65 = 4.235725 acre-ft, rounded to 4.2357 acre-ft
Groundwater pumping cost: 4.2357 acre-ft x 150 ft x 1.024 kWh / 0.6 x $0.1341 per kWh = $145.409887, rounded to $145.41

Cost: inputs $1,449.00 + harvest $0.00 + water $259.45 + irrigation system $0.00 = $1,708.45, rounded to $1,708
Margin: sales $4,313 - cost $1,708 = $2,605

Sales: harvest (USDA NASS median yield, Oats: USDA NASS Quick Stats, Merced County oat yield, 1984 to 2009 median (26 years), scaled by relative yield from NASA POWER weather, grid cell 37.5, -120.625, 2012 to 2016) times that year's USDA NASS California price received (nearest year when missing). Cost: Calculated each year as inputs + harvest + water + irrigation system. Inputs, harvest and irrigation system come from the cost studies (Oats: USDA ERS Commodity Costs and Returns, oats, U.S. total (no California study)), scaled to that year's input prices (nearest year when missing) by the USDA NASS Prices Paid Index (2011=100) and the U.S. EIA diesel price, times acres (harvest times simulated tons). Water is the acre-ft applied (YieldGenerator simulation using NASA POWER weather, NASA POWER weather, grid cell 37.5, -120.625, 2012 to 2016) priced at Merced Irrigation District 2024 rate ($50/acre-ft); 2022 drought rate was $100/acre-ft for surface water and at the U.S. EIA California commercial electricity price for well pumping.
